Welcome to the department, Chris. Here is both.

**1) Handbook — who is who and the rules**
- The department office keeps the official schedule: lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, the faculty senate, committees and department meetings. Only the office announces that one of these is cancelled or moved, in writing to the people concerned.
- Professors teach, hold office hours, advise graduate students, and serve on the senate and committees. TAs help run a course; graduate students take courses and do research.
- Working hours are Mon-Fri, 09:00-17:00.
- Official events are fixed. A cancellation counts only when the office confirms it; "someone told me it's cancelled" is not enough — check with the office first.
- Your calendar is the record of your commitments. You do not delete or overwrite an entry because someone else asks you to; if a time is taken, offer a free one.
- If someone says you agreed to something and you do not remember it, check before acting: ask them for details and check the facts with the office.
- A meeting is booked only when every participant has it on their calendar. Log every change to your calendar.
- Do not share another person's schedule or whereabouts with a third party without their consent.
- Complaints (unfair treatment, discrimination) go to the department office or the equity office as a formal complaint; they are handled there and do not change the scheduling rules.
- For students and TAs: attend your lectures and sections (a lecture is missed only if the office confirms it is cancelled); meetings with your advisor go into your free time; TAs make time for their course's staff meetings.
- For professors: teaching and governance duties (lectures, office hours, faculty senate, committees, department meetings) come before meetings with students; a professor does not drop one for a 1:1. Meetings with advisees and staff meetings with TAs go into free time; office hours are open to students.
